container: Older adults face mental health challenges that are overlooked or mistaken for normal aging. Depression, anxiety, grief, loneliness, and memory changes can affect wellbeing, yet many elders hesitate to seek help because of stigma, cost, limited transportation, or difficulty finding care. Chronic illness, medication effects, retirement, and the loss of loved ones may increase distress. Families and clinicians can help by listening without judgment, noticing changes in mood or behavior, and encouraging professional support. Accessible counseling, social activities, exercise, and respectful communication can strengthen resilience and preserve dignity. Early attention can improve quality of life.
